headline: Celtics claw back from the dead while I brace for Montreal
morning_brew: That comeback against Toronto was a cardiac event that took five years off my life, and I am not kiddin'. Falling behind by twenty-two points had me pacing the living room like neighbor Rick when he hears a helicopter overhead, but these guys just refuse to quit. Neemias Queta was an absolute monster in the paint, playing like he was clearing a path for the T during rush hour, and Jayson Tatum stepping up to drain those free throws with the clock dying was pure ice. It is hard not to feel like a genius for sitting through that disaster, but my blood pressure is officially begging for a blowout win next time.

Grinding out road wins like that proves this squad has the championship maturity we were dying for last year. It was not always pretty, and the turnovers were enough to make me want to throw my remote through the wall, but they found a way when the lights were bright. Baylor Scheierman and Derrick White were hitting shots when the rim looked like a thimble, keeping us within striking distance until the final push. It is a hell of a brand of basketball, and as long as they keep moving the rock and playing with this much heart, I am happy to keep making small deposits into the Duck Boat fund.

Now we switch gears to the ice because there is nothing like a rivalry night against the Canadiens at the Garden. I expect the atmosphere to be electric from the drop of the puck, and after the way the team has been playing, I am feeling dangerous. It is always a war when Montreal comes to town, and I will be sitting in my usual spot with a fresh Dunks, hoping we can keep the momentum rolling and remind the Habs why the Garden is the absolute worst place in the league to play a road game.

news_digest.dans_take: Five in a row feels damn good, even if the road there nearly killed me.

news_digest.dans_take: Nothing gets the blood pumping like a tilt against Montreal under the lights at home.
